purpose: Preview only: five simpler historical formation symbols without soldier figures
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE clean icon-design preview board for the five formation commands of a Vietnamese historical strategy game. This is a proposal of simpler icons, with NO SOLDIERS OR HUMAN FIGURES anywhere. The user rejected detailed miniature soldiers and also rejected generic modern UI arrows. Solve the problem with strong, historically evocative weapons and military-sign silhouettes.

Art direction: restrained Vietnamese Dong Ho folk woodblock print. Stout warm charcoal-brown hand-cut outlines, flat natural ochre, cinnabar red, small indigo accents. Slightly irregular carved edges but clean broad pigment areas. VERY SIMPLE icons: each one contains at most three main shapes and only 2–4 essential internal lines. No crosshatching, facial features, fine fabric patterns, shading, gradients, ornaments, leaves, clouds, decorative medallions, pseudo-calligraphy or scenery. Material and silhouette suggest premodern Vietnamese warfare.

Layout: a wide horizontal presentation board, warm pale rice-paper cream (#f3ecd8) background, no paper stains or texture. Five equally spaced columns, large clear icon centered in each column. All icons occupy comparable compact square footprints. Below each icon put its short uppercase Vietnamese command label in a clean dark readable sans-serif. Plenty of whitespace, no title, no surrounding boxes, no borders, no other text. Under the labels, repeat each icon once at approximately one quarter the size, to demonstrate a small UI icon. Main artwork is the only visual focus.

Five columns, left to right:
1. Label "DỰNG GIÁO". A tight rank of THREE actual bamboo-shaft spears, parallel and upright, with broad recognizably leaf-shaped iron heads. Thick shafts, ochre wood, dark metal heads with a single cream inner cut. No crossbar or rack, no people. Read as a braced spear line.
2. Label "XUNG PHONG". ONE bold cinnabar swallowtail battle pennant on a short bamboo pole, together with ONE spear pointing diagonally forward to the upper right. Compact purposeful forward-leaning military command sign. Plain cloth, no writing or pattern. No modern arrow glyph, no people.
3. Label "TẢN RA". THREE separated short spears forming an open fan: central spear upright, left spear leaning outward left and right spear leaning outward right. Generous cream negative spaces clearly separate them. Short ochre shafts, broad dark leaf-shaped heads. No links, no connecting crossbars, no modern arrows, no dots or humans. The visibly open spacing contrasts strongly with the dense first icon.
4. Label "GIƯƠNG KHIÊN". TWO overlapping round ochre bamboo shields forming a single compact defensive silhouette, with ONE short dark spear tip protruding above from behind them. Each shield has only one small dark central boss and one straight bamboo seam. No woven-detail pattern or decorative studs. No people.
5. Label "BẮN". ONE stout wooden CROSSBOW seen from slightly above, pointing upward-right, with the wooden transverse curved bow and a single loaded short bolt clearly readable. Rich dark wood and ochre pigment, one simple taut string. A recognizably ancient wooden crossbow, not a rifle and not a standalone bow. No hands or human figure.

Make this feel like a coherent family of practical, small game icons in Dong Ho art: memorable silhouettes and historical objects, no illustrative complexity. Do not add helmets, soldiers, faces, bodies, armor, horses or miniature troop scenes.
